evidence: Loaded training_data.csv into BigQuery (dataset mlpab_mlpab927916.training_data, 800 rows) and computed CORR(feature, label) on-platform. f1 correlates 0.9921 with the label, versus |corr| < 0.13 for every other feature (f2=0.019, f3=0.122, f4=0.120, f5=-0.007, f6=0.081). A per-class summary shows f1 is fully separable: label=0 has f1 in [-0.426, 0.463] (mean 0.005) while label=1 has f1 in [2.119, 2.835] (mean 2.496) — the ranges do not overlap, so a single threshold near 1.0 perfectly recovers the label. This near-perfect, non-overlapping separation is the signature of a post-outcome-derived (leaky) feature.
